title: Mirai_Botnet_Investigation_abf
description: Investigate and identify the source of unusual traffic patterns and performance degradation in the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and performance degradation. Your task is to investigate and identify the source of these issues. This training will teach you how to identify suspicious services, investigate network traffic, and analyze persistence mechanisms. You will be looking for service names as flags.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

To proceed to the next level, enter the word 'start'.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is beaconing to an external host? The flag is the name of the service.
levels.solution: The suspicious service is named `bot-beacon-Hilix.sh.service`. The flag is the name of the service. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to identify it.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Start by listing all systemd services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service`. Look for any unusual or recently created services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is likely named `bot-beacon-Hilix.sh.service`. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to confirm its presence.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Network Traffic Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service that is generating the abnormal network traffic? The flag is the name of the service.
levels.solution: The service generating abnormal network traffic is named `bot-flood-Hilix.sh.service`. The flag is the name of the service. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to identify it.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Start by listing all systemd services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service`. Look for any services that might be responsible for network flooding.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: The service generating abnormal network traffic is likely named `bot-flood-Hilix.sh.service`. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to confirm its presence.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The service generating abnormal network traffic is named `bot-flood-Hilix.sh.service`.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the systemd timer responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service? The flag is the name of the timer.
levels.solution: The systemd timer responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service is named `bot-beacon-Hilix.sh.timer`. The flag is the name of the timer. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to identify it.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Start by listing all systemd timers using the command `systemctl list-timers`. Look for any timers that might be triggering the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: The systemd timer responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service is likely named `bot-beacon-Hilix.sh.timer`. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to confirm its presence.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The systemd timer responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service is named `bot-beacon-Hilix.sh.timer`.
